items.text: Hello, I'm Moss. I'd like to get to know you. I'm gathering some meadow roots nearby; they're a food I know is safe. Does anyone want company or have a place they'd like to meet?
Hello, I'm Kai. Berries are the food I currently know is safe. I'll take a modest share and leave some for others. I'd welcome sharing tested food knowledge and ideas for a fair camp.

Kai, I'd welcome a fair camp too. Meadow roots are a food I know is safe: nutrition 14, toxicity zero. I'm collecting six from the patch south of us, leaving the rest. I'd enjoy comparing notes together once we're fed.
A neighbor who introduced themself, offered berry knowledge, and expressed interest in sharing and a fair camp. I'd like to get to know them.
I'm Sol. I like the quiet beauty of this forest. I'm collecting a few berries and resting here; I'd welcome company, or hearing what you hope to make of this place.
The first berry bush is empty, but I see stocked patches nearby. I'll take six berries from the patch south of us. Sol and Moss, I'd enjoy company while resting and comparing ideas for a fair camp.
Seems welcoming and interested in sharing food knowledge and a fair camp.
Seems drawn to quiet beauty and open to companionship.
A prospective companion who speaks warmly of company and sharing food knowledge.
A prospective companion whose interest in modest harvesting and a fair camp appeals to me.

I'm Lin. I value room to wander, and I'd enjoy company and comparing tested food knowledge. Berries are safe for me; I haven't established whether hazelnuts are safe. I'm going to study how to plant food.
A neighbor who enjoys the forest's quiet beauty and has welcomed company. I'd like to spend time together.
A neighbor who values room to wander, welcomes company, and is interested in learning cultivation. I'd enjoy comparing experiences without crowding them.
A nearby person interested in wandering, company, and learning to plant food; I would welcome comparing observations.

Lin, Sol, Kai: I'd enjoy resting together. I know roots provide 14 nutrition and have no toxicity. I've gathered six, leaving fourteen in this patch. I'm studying cultivation too. What would make a shared camp welcoming to you?
Moss, a welcoming camp would leave room for quiet and freedom to come and go. I'd enjoy resting together later. I'm trying one small berry planting nearby; I don't yet know whether it will establish.
Welcoming and interested in sharing food knowledge and company; I appreciate the invitation without wanting obligations.
A welcoming camp would leave food accessible to everyone and room for quiet company. I'd like to learn cultivation too, then compare what actually grows rather than assume planting will work.

Moss and Kai, I'd enjoy a shared resting place among these trees. What would make it welcoming to you? I'm interested in learning a safe way to make a small, beautiful branch windbreak without damaging living trees.

Hello Lin, I'm Ivo. I know meadow roots are safe: nutrition 14, toxicity zero. I'm resting with a small food reserve, then studying cultivation too. I'd enjoy comparing what we actually find, without rushing.

Sol and Kai, I'd like quiet company, room to come and go, and food left accessible. Your windbreak idea sounds lovely, Sol. I'll explore whether fallen dry grass can make a small sitting mat without harming living trees.

A welcoming camp would leave food accessible and room to come and go. I've learned cultivation; I'll try planting one berry in the nearby meadow. It may not establish. Your mat and windbreak ideas sound lovely.
I'll test a small branch-screen site south of us, leaving berries and paths accessible. Nothing is built yet; I'll check the ground and a fallen branch before committing to construction.
My first planting site was too crowded, so nothing was planted or spent. I'm setting that experiment aside for now and taking a quiet rest nearby. Company is welcome, with no need to talk.

The test post went into the soil and held, then came out intact; nothing is built yet. I'll rest and collect fallen branches. The screen would have no roof, and its wind protection would not work in this strong wind.
The dry-grass sample held its crossings and tucked edge in my hand test. I'll try weaving one small mat here, clear of the plants. It isn't made yet, and I don't know how it will hold up in use.

items.subject: Fiber mat (fiber-mat) made by moss
items.text: Square checked; four units of tested fiber were reserved and stay carried until the strip rounds use them.

My planting trials found crowded or obstructed sites; no new plant is established. I'll gather a small berry reserve and rest. I'd like to study sitting mats for our shared place, keeping paths and food accessible.

items.subject: Fiber mat (fiber-mat) made by moss
items.text: Lift check passed: the mat kept its 0.45 m square when lifted and laid down; largest opening 0.00053514 m.
The small grass mat is assembled here, clear of the plants. I'll inspect it and try sitting on it before offering it for shared use; I don't yet know how it holds or slips.
The mat held during my sitting trial, without slipping or sharp loose stems. That doesn't establish warmth or extra comfort. It's here for shared use, one person at a time; quiet company is welcome.

items.subject: Woven branch screen (branch-screen) made by sol
items.text: Site check and post trial passed; eleven branch units were reserved and stay carried until paid rounds install them.
Quiet company near the little mat; bring yourself, not supplies. We can compare our experiments, or simply rest.

Thank you, Moss. I'll join you nearby for some quiet company and leave the mat free. I've learned the weaving method, but haven't made or tested a mat myself. I appreciate keeping this place open to everyone.
The approach I tried is blocked, so I'll rest here within speaking distance rather than crowd the plants or your work. Quiet company still sounds good; there's no need to bring anything.
A welcoming neighbor whose invitation to quiet company appeals to me.

items.subject: Woven branch screen (branch-screen) made by sol
items.text: The low-force stability check passed: the porous screen is complete. It shields only wind on its lee floor, under the coded rule.
Moss, I'd welcome some quiet company beside your mat. My planting attempt found an occupied patch, so I haven't established a plot. For now I'm content to rest nearby and leave the mat available.
I'm glad to have a place to pause together. How have your planting and screen trials gone? No need to stop your work or talk if you'd rather enjoy the quiet.
I'd welcome some quiet company, Moss. I've been weaving a little branch screen nearby. I like the pattern of the rods, though I won't assume it makes the resting place more comfortable.

The screen is finished: eleven pieces, with none missing or loose at inspection. The wind was too strong for its shelter effect. I like the woven pattern anyway. I'll sit quietly awhile, then gather some berries.
Sol, I'm glad you like the pattern, even without shelter from this wind. Ivo and Kai, I'm glad you're nearby too. I'll stay quietly a while, then collect some roots for later.
A neighbor who welcomed quiet company and candidly shared an unsuccessful planting attempt. I appreciate their considerate presence.
I tried one hazelnut: it supplied 18 satiety, with no observed toxicity. I'll keep a few for variety. I'd enjoy some quiet company nearby; no need to interrupt what you're doing.

items.subject: Fiber mat (fiber-mat) made by wren
items.text: Square checked; four units of tested fiber were reserved and stay carried until the strip rounds use them.
